name: City Council Meeting - Feb 27, 2024
agenda_text:
TORRANCE CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
  FEBRUARY 27, 2024
  ADJOURNED REGULAR MEETING
  5:00 P.M. - CLOSED SESSION
  6:30 P.M. - REGULAR BUSINESS BEGINS
  IN COUNCIL CHAMBER AT 3031 TORRANCE BL.

  CITY COUNCIL MAY TAKE ACTION ON ANY ITEM LISTED ON THE AGENDA

City Council Agenda 02-27-24

OPENING CEREMONIES

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

ROLL CALL : Councilmembers Griffiths, Kaji, Kalani, Lewis, Mattucci, Sheikh, and Mayor
Chen

14.  CLOSED SESSION

  14A. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION (California
  Government Code §54956.9(d)(1)):
  1)  Deborah Walls v. City of Torrance, et al.  LASC Case No. 24TRCV00286
  2)  Sling Flying Club, LLC, DBA Sling Pilot Academy v. City of Torrance, et al. LASC Case
  No. 23STCP04538
  3)  Eric Hickman v. City of Torrance  LASC Case No. 19STCV37386
  14A - STAFF REPORT

  14B. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (California Government Code
  §54957.6): Agency Negotiator: Aram Chaparyan Employee
  Organization/Association:
  1. Certain Full-Time Salaried and Hourly Employees
  2. Certain Part-Time Hourly Employees
  3. Crossing Guards
  4. Elected Officials
  5. Engineers and Torrance Fiscal Employees Association
  6. Executive & Management Employees
  7. Police & Fire Trainees
  8. Safety Management Employees
  9. Torrance City Employees Association
  10. Fire Safety Management
  11. Torrance Fire Fighters Association
  12. Torrance Library Employees Association
  13. Torrance Municipal Employees/AFSCME Local 1117 AFL-CIO
  14. Torrance Police Commanders Association (TPCA)
  15. Torrance Police Officers Association
  16. Torrance Professional Parks & Recreation Employees Organization
  17. Torrance Professional & Supervisory Association
  18. Torrance Recurrent Recreational Employees Organization
  19. City Treasurer
  20. City Clerk
  21. City Attorney
  22. City Manager

  14C. PUBLIC EMPLOYEE DISCIPLINE/DISMISSAL/RELEASE (California Government
  Code §54957)

  14D. PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION (California Government Code
  §54957(b)(1)): Title: City Attorney
   14E. REAL PROPERTY – CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR
  (California Government Code §54956.8):
  1)  Property: 20500 Madrona Avenue, Torrance, CA 90503 Agency Negotiator: Aram
  Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and California Water Service Company
  Under Negotiation: Terms and conditions of easement
  2)  Property: 20500 Madrona Avenue, Torrance, CA 90503 Agency Negotiator: Aram
  Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and Water Replenishment District
  Under Negotiation: Price and terms and conditions of lease
  3)  Property: 25225 Crenshaw Boulevard, Torrance, CA 90505 Agency Negotiator: Aram
  Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and Armstrong Garden Centers, Inc.
  Under Negotiation: Price and terms and conditions of lease

RECESSED TO CLOSED SESSION - Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9 (d)(1)

10.  HEARINGS

  10A. City Manager – Conduct Closed Hearing on the Appeal of the Civil Service
  Commission Decision Sustaining the Termination of a Police Services Officer.
  Consideration of Public Employee Discipline Will Be Conducted in Closed
  Session Per California Government Code Section 54957(B)(1), Unless the
  Employee Requests to Have the Appeal Conducted in Public Session. The
  Deliberation of this Matter by the City Council Will Occur in Closed Session.
  Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council conduct a closed hearing to
  consider an appeal of the Civil Service Commission’s decision sustaining the termination of
  a Police Services Officer, unless the employee requests to have the hearing in public
  session and that the City Council’s deliberation of this matter shall occur in closed session.
  10A - STAFF REPORT

RECONVENED IN PUBLIC SESSION

2.  FLAG SALUTE: Councilmember Griffiths

  NON SECTARIAN INVOCATION: Councilmember Kalani

3.  REPORT OF THE CITY CLERK ON THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA The agenda was
  posted on the Public Notice Board at 3031 Torrance Bl. and on the City’s Website on
  Wednesday, February 21, 2024 /s/ Rebecca Poirier.
  3 - AFFIDAVIT

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READING OF RESOLUTIONS AND ORDINANCES AFTER
NUMBER & TITLE – See Council Rules of Order Section 2.11 (Resolution 2006-65)

4.  ANNOUNCEMENT OF WITHDRAWN, DEFERRED, AND/OR SUPPLEMENTAL ITEMS

5.  COUNCIL COMMITTEE MEETINGS AND ANNOUNCEMENTS

6.  COMMUNITY MATTERS

  6A. City Manager – Appoint Torrance Representative to the South Bay Workforce
  Investment Board.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council appoint Kimberley Miller to serve on
  the South Bay Workforce Investment Board.
  6A - STAFF REPORT

  6B. PROCLAMATION declaring March 7 - 14, 2024 as California Arbor Week in the
  City of Torrance.
  6B - STAFF REPORT

  6C. PROCLAMATION declaring March 2024 as American Red Cross Month in the City
  of Torrance.
  6C - STAFF REPORT
 7.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #1 (Limited up to a 15 minute period) This portion of the
  meeting is reserved for comment on items under the Consent Calendar or items that
  are not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M. Brown Act, City Council cannot act on
  items raised during public comment, but may respond briefly to statements made or
  questions posed; request clarification; or refer the item to staff. Speakers under Orals
  are limited to either Oral Communications #1 or Oral Communications #2 and no
  longer than 1 minute per speaker. Time starts when you step up to the microphone. If
  presenting handout material to Council, please provide 11 copies to the City Clerk
  before speaking.
  PUBLIC COMMENT
  PUBLIC COMMENT RECEIVED AFTER 5:30 P.M. ON 02/26/24 AND BEFORE 10:58
  P.M.ON 02/27/24

8.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  Matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion and one
  vote. There will be no separate discussion of these items. If discussion is desired, that item will be removed by
  a Councilmember from the Consent Calendar and considered separately..

  8A. City Clerk – Approve City Council Minutes. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Clerk that City Council approve the City Council minutes of
  February 6, 2024.

  8B. Community Services – Consider and Approve Little Free Library Book-Sharing
  Pilot Program at Various City Parks and Authorize In-Kind Services. Expenditure:
  $1,730 (General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Community Services Director that City Council:
  1) Consider and approve a little free library book-sharing pilot program at various City
  parks; and
  2) Authorize in-kind services in the amount of $1,730 to install posts for eight (8) little
  library boxes.
  8B - STAFF REPORT

  8C. City Treasurer – Accept and File Investment Report for the Month of November
  2023. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Treasurer that City Council accept and file the Investment
  Report for the month of November 2023.
  8C - STAFF REPORT

  8D. City Treasurer – Accept and File Investment Report for the Month of December
  2023. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Treasurer that City Council accept and file the Investment
  Report for the month of December 2023.
  8D - STAFF REPORT

9.  ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS

  9A. Public Works – Adopt Categorical Exemption Under California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) Section 15301(c) – Existing Facilities (Class 1), Approve
  Plans and Specifications, Appropriate Funds, and Award Public Works
  Agreement for the Residential and Arterial Pavement Improvement Program, I-
  159/I-139. Expenditure: $21,252,480 (General Fund and Non-General Funds).
  Recommendation of the Public Works Director that City Council:
  1) Adopt a categorical exemption, pursuant to Section 15301(c) of the guidelines
  implementing CEQA for the Residential and Arterial Pavement Improvement Program,
  I-159/I-139 (B2023-42); and
  2) Approve the plans and specifications for the Residential and Arterial Pavement
  Improvement Program, I-159/I-139 (B2023-42); and
  3) Appropriate $46,000 from the Airport Fund’s fund balance to the Arterial Pavement
  Improvement Program, I-139; and
  4) Award a public works agreement to All American Asphalt of Corona, CA (B2023-42) in
  the amount of $18,480,420 and authorize a 15% contingency in the amount of
  $2,772,060 for construction of the Residential and Arterial Pavement Improvement
  Program, I-159/I-139 for a two-year period beginning February 27, 2024, and ending
   February 26, 2026.
  9A - STAFF REPORT

9B. Public Works – Approve First Amendment to Public Works Agreement for Van
  Ness Water Wells Transmission Main, I-145. Expenditure: $1,000,000 (Non-
  General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Public Works Director that City Council approve a first amendment
  to the public works agreement with Vido Artukovich & Son, Inc. / Vidmar, Inc., a California
  joint venture of South El Monte, CA (C2022-054) in the amount of $1,000,000, for a new
  not-to-exceed amount of $15,832,149.85, to provide construction services for the Van Ness
  Water Wells Transmission Main, I-145 and to extend the term for an additional one-year
  period beginning April 12, 2024 and ending April 11, 2025.
  9B - STAFF REPORT

9C. City Clerk, City Manager, and City Attorney – Consider and Give Direction on
  Potential City Charter Amendments. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Clerk, City Manager, and City Attorney that City Council:
  1) Direct staff on public hearing dates for potential City Charter amendments; and
  2) Direct staff on potential amendments to the City Charter.
  9C - STAFF REPORT PART 1
  9C - STAFF REPORT PART 2
  9C - STAFF REPORT PART 3
  9C - STAFF REPORT PART 4
  9C - STAFF REPORT PART 5
  9C - SUPPLEMENTAL

9D. Finance - Discuss and Provide Direction Regarding Forensic Review of Financial
  Processes. Expenditure: None.
  In response to an oral request by Councilmember Jon Kaji with City Council concurrence, it
  is the recommendation of the Finance Director that City Council provide direction regarding
  a forensic review of financial processes.
  9D - STAFF REPORT

9E.  City Manager – Adopt RESOLUTION Pursuant to Memorandum of Understanding
  (MOU) Setting Forth Hours, Wages, and Working Conditions for Torrance Police
  Officers Association (TPOA). Expenditure: $5,769,258 (General Fund:
  Approximately $3,061,239 Annually).
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council adopt a RESOLUTION pursuant to
  the memorandum of understanding (MOU) setting forth the hours, wages, and working
  conditions for employees represented by the Torrance Police Officers Association (TPOA)
  for the period beginning January 1, 2024, and ending December 31, 2025.
  9E - STAFF REPORT

9F.  City Manager – Adopt RESOLUTION Setting Forth Changes to Hours, Wages, and
  Working Conditions for Police Trainee. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council adopt a RESOLUTION amending
  Resolution No. 2023-06 setting forth changes to the hours, wages, and working conditions
  for Police Trainee regarding pay ranges and health insurance contributions.
  9F - STAFF REPORT

9G. City Manager - Consider and Approve Reinstatement of Membership with League
  of California Cities. Expenditure: $35,522.75 (General Fund).
  In response to an oral request by Mayor George Chen with City Council concurrence, it is
  the recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Consider and approve reinstatement of membership with the League of California
  Cities; and
  2) Appropriate $35,522.75 from the General Fund’s fund balance to the City Council’s
  fiscal year 2023-24 operating budget.
  9G - STAFF REPORT
  9G - SUPPLEMENTAL

9H. City Manager and Community Services – Provide Direction on Los Angeles
  Dodgers Game Date, Approve Purchase of 1,000 Tickets, Provide Direction on
   Add-On Options, and Authorize Resale of Tickets to Torrance Community
  Members. Expenditure: Not-to-Exceed $31,710 (General Fund).
  Recommendation of the City Manager and Community Services Director that City Council:
  1) Provide direction on selecting one of three Los Angeles Dodgers game date options
  and approve the purchase of 1,000 tickets for an amount not-to-exceed $31,010; and
  2) Provide direction on the purchase of an on-field photo opportunity for up to 30 people
  for an amount not-to-exceed $200; and
  3) Provide direction on the purchase of a visiting team batting practice experience for up
  to 30 people for an amount not-to-exceed $500; and
  4) Authorize the resale of 1,000 Los Angeles Dodgers game tickets to Torrance
  community members at $15.00 per ticket.
  9H - STAFF REPORT
  9H - SUPPLEMENTAL

  9I.  Community Services – Discuss and Provide Direction Regarding 2024 City-
  Sponsored 4th of July Fireworks Show. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Services Director that City Council discuss and provide
  direction regarding a City-sponsored 4th of July fireworks show at the Torrance Civic Center
  on Thursday, July 4, 2024.
  9I - STAFF REPORT

11.  AGENCY AGENDAS – None Scheduled.

12.  2ND READING ORDINANCES – None Scheduled.

13.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #2 (Limited up to a 15 minute period) Council Order – Kaji,
  Kalani, Lewis, Mattucci, Griffiths, Mayor Chen This portion of the meeting is reserved
  for comment on items not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M. Brown Act, City Council
  cannot act on items raised during public comment, but may respond briefly to
  statements made or questions posed; request clarification; or refer the item to staff.
  Speakers under Orals are limited to either Oral Communications #1 or Oral
  Communications #2 and no longer than 1 minute per speaker. Time starts when you
  step up to the microphone. If presenting handout material to Council, please provide
  11 copies to the City Clerk before speaking.

RECESSED TO CLOSED SESSION - Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9 (d)(1)

RECONVENED IN PUBLIC SESSION

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  15A. Adjournment of City Council meeting to Tuesday, March 12, 2024, at 5:00 p.m. for
  closed session, with regular business commencing at 6:30 p.m. in the Council
  Chamber. Tuesday, March 5, 2024, is a Council Dark Night.
  15A - STAFF REPORT
